subject: geography
title: ZIMSEC O-Level Geography

officialDocument.title: Geography Syllabus, Forms 1 - 4, 2015 - 2022 (Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education, Curriculum Development Unit), examined by ZIMSEC at O Level
officialDocument.publisher: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (Curriculum Development Unit) / Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC)

sourceNote: Topic headings and numbers (7.1 to 7.12) are transcribed from the scope and sequence (section 7) of the Ministry's Geography Syllabus Forms 1 - 4 (2015 - 2022); the sub-topics group the scope-and-sequence items and the competency-matrix topics of each Form, and each sub-topic's description names its Form(s). Sub-topic codes (7.1.1, ...) and objective codes are ours, not the board's. Learning-objective statements are our own paraphrase of the competency matrix; no syllabus text is reproduced.
notes: Source (read 2026-10-08): the Mashonaland West provincial education office's copy of the Ministry document, file 'GEOGRAPPHY SYLLABUS new.pdf' (http://www.mopsemashwest.gov.zw/files/GEOGRAPPHY%20SYLLABUS%20new.pdf; the site's https certificate has expired, so the https form of the URL is recorded), read through a pdftotext rendering. The cover prints 'Geography Syllabus, Forms 1 - 4, 2015-2022' (Curriculum Development Unit, 2015; print date 26 October 2016). The scope-and-sequence and competency-matrix tables are scrambled in the text rendering, so absence of an item is less certain than its presence. Check every heading and objective against a clean copy from ZIMSEC.
Subject code: not printed in the document. ZIMSEC O-Level Geography is commonly cited as 4022; confirm it (code left null).

Version dates: assumed first examined in November 2018 (effectiveFrom 2018-01-01), as for the other 2015-2022 files. Under the Heritage-Based Curriculum (2024-2030) new syllabi were issued; confirm which syllabus the November 2026 and later O-Level Geography examinations use, set effectiveTo, and create a new version file when a new syllabus replaces this one.

Assessment (9.0) as read: continuous assessment 40% (a practical assignment, a theory test and a project in each of Forms 1 to 4; each task marked out of 100) and summative examination 60%. Paper 1: 40 compulsory multiple-choice items on all topics, 1 hour 30 minutes, 40 marks, 20%. Paper 2: structured free-response and data-response questions, 2 hours 30 minutes, 100 marks, 40%; nine questions, three in each of Sections A, B and C; candidates answer four (one from each section and one more from any section), 25 marks each. The weightings on the components are shares of the whole qualification; continuous assessment is not a component here.

Inconsistency to check: the paper description says Paper 2 has nine questions (three per section) but the content specification grid lists four questions in each of Section A (Physical Environment), Section B (Economic Geography) and Section C (Population, Settlement, Transport and Trade), twelve in all. Confirm with a recent Paper 2.

Specification grid as read: skills weighting Paper 1 / Paper 2 = knowledge and comprehension 40% / 30%, skills and application 40% / 40%, judgement and decision-making 20% / 30%. Paper 1 content grid (scrambled, totals reconstructed): Topographical Map Work 12 items, Physical Environment 13, Economic Geography 8, Population, Settlement, Transport and Trade 7 (total 40); skill 1 14 items (35%), skill 2 17 (42.5%), skill 3 9 (22.5%). Map work is assessed in Paper 1 only according to the grid. The grid does not say which topics count as Physical Environment and which as Economic Geography; our mock blueprints assume Physical = topics 7.1-7.3 and 7.8, Economic = 7.4, 7.5, 7.7, 7.9 and 7.10, and Section C = 7.11 and 7.12. Confirm.

Numbering in the competency matrix: Forms 1 to 3 follow the topic list (Topics 1 to 12), but the Form 4 matrix renumbers the topics it covers (Topic 5 = GIS, 6 = Minerals and mining, 7 = Environmental management, 8 = Agriculture, 9 = Industry, 10 = Settlement and population) and has no Form 4 entries for natural resources, energy or transport and trade. The tree follows the topic list (6.1-6.12) and the scope and sequence (7.1-7.12).

Scope and sequence versus competency matrix: continental drift is listed under Form 2 in the scope and sequence but appears in the Form 3 matrix; 'Patterns and networks' (Form 2 map work) has no matrix entry beyond land-use patterns; 'Remote sensing (photo interpretation)' (Form 3) appears in the matrix only as the electromagnetic spectrum applied to photographs; Form 3 transport and trade has only regional imbalances and trading blocs.

Agro-ecological regions: the Form 2 matrix lists 'Regions 1 - 6'. Zimbabwe's natural regions are conventionally numbered I to V with Region II divided into IIa and IIb (six units); lessons use the I-V (IIa/IIb) convention. Confirm.

Mapwork resources: the platform cannot show Ordnance-survey-style map extracts, so map-work content uses grid-square tables and described extracts; check that Paper 1 map-work practice is still realistic.

components.name: Paper 1: Multiple choice
components.description: 40 compulsory multiple-choice items set on all syllabus topics (topographical map work, physical environment, economic geography, and population, settlement, transport and trade).

components.name: Paper 2: Structured free-response and data response
components.description: Nine structured free-response and data-response questions of 25 marks: three in Section A (physical environment), three in Section B (economic geography) and three in Section C (population, settlement, transport and trade). Candidates answer four: one from each section and one more from any section.

topics.name: Weather and climate
topics.description: Topic 1 of the scope and sequence: weather elements, data and forecasting (Form 1), hazards and the climate of Zimbabwe (Form 2), air masses and world climates (Form 3), depressions, cyclones and climate change (Form 4).

children.name: Weather elements, instruments and the weather station
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: Distinguish between weather and climate and list the elements of weather.
Describe the instruments used to measure each element and read and record weather data.
Identify the factors that influence where a weather station is sited and describe the Stevenson screen.

children.name: Weather and climatic data
children.description: Form 1 (weather tables, graphs, maps and statistics) and Form 3 (interpretation of climatic data).

objectives.text: Draw weather tables and graphs from recorded data.
Calculate weather statistics such as means, ranges and totals.
Interpret climatic graphs and tables.

children.name: Precipitation and types of rainfall
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: Identify the forms of precipitation.
Describe how rain forms.
Draw annotated diagrams of relief, convectional and frontal rainfall.

children.name: Synoptic charts and weather forecasting
children.description: Form 1: synoptic symbols and charts, the meaning and importance of forecasting, indigenous forecasting.

objectives.text: Interpret synoptic symbols and simple weather maps.
Explain what weather forecasting is and why it is important.
Describe how indigenous knowledge systems are used to forecast weather.

children.name: Weather hazards and the influence of people on weather
children.description: Form 2: floods, lightning and drought; effects of activities such as deforestation, dam building and industrialisation on weather.

objectives.text: Outline weather hazards and describe their causes and effects.
Suggest measures to reduce the impact of weather hazards.
Describe and evaluate how human activities change local weather.

children.name: The climate of Zimbabwe and climate variability
children.description: Form 2: climatic zones and patterns of Zimbabwe; temperature and rainfall anomalies.

objectives.text: Describe Zimbabwe's climatic zones and relate them to economic activities.
Describe climate variability in Zimbabwe and its effects.
Suggest solutions to the effects of climate variability.

children.name: Air masses and the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone
children.description: Form 3: classification and characteristics of air masses; air masses affecting Zimbabwe and southern Africa; the ITCZ.

objectives.text: Describe and classify air masses and their characteristics.
Describe the weather associated with the air masses that affect Zimbabwe and southern Africa.
Describe the position of the ITCZ in January and July and the weather associated with it.

children.name: Climatic types on a global scale
children.description: Form 3: tropical, warm temperate and polar climates.

objectives.text: Explain the basis for classifying climates on a global scale.
Describe the characteristics and distribution of the world's main climatic regions.

children.name: Temperate depressions and frontal systems
children.description: Form 4.

objectives.text: Describe the factors that influence the development and distribution of temperate depressions.
Describe the weather associated with different types of front.

children.name: Tropical cyclones
children.description: Form 4.

objectives.text: Discuss the distribution and development of tropical cyclones.
Explain the weather conditions and hazards associated with tropical cyclones.

children.name: People's influence on climate and climate change
children.description: Form 4: human influence on climate (for example afforestation, desertification, dam construction); the nature, causes and effects of climate change in Zimbabwe and the world; adaptation and mitigation.

objectives.text: Identify human activities that influence climate.
Describe the nature, causes and effects of climate change in Zimbabwe and the world.
Identify ways of adapting to and mitigating climate change.

topics.name: Landforms and landscape processes
topics.description: Topic 2 of the scope and sequence: landforms (Form 1), rocks, weathering and the Earth's structure (Form 2), tectonic processes (Form 3), river and wind landforms and hazards (Form 4).

children.name: Landforms and their benefits
children.description: Form 1: landforms in the local area, Zimbabwe, Africa and the world.

objectives.text: Identify and describe landforms in the local area, Zimbabwe, Africa and the world.
Explain the benefits of landforms and distinguish between landforms and landscape.

children.name: Rocks
children.description: Form 2: igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks and their origin.

objectives.text: Identify the main rock types and describe how each forms.
Describe the characteristics of rocks within each type and classify rocks.

children.name: Weathering of rocks and resulting landforms
children.description: Form 2: physical (mechanical) and chemical weathering; granitic and karst landforms. Mass wasting is listed under Form 4 hazards and is taught with weathering here.

objectives.text: Describe the main types of weathering and distinguish mechanical from chemical weathering.
Describe landforms that result from weathering, including granite and karst landforms.

children.name: The internal structure of the Earth, continental drift and plate tectonics
children.description: Form 2 (internal structure; continental drift in the scope and sequence) and Form 3 (continental drift and plate tectonics in the competency matrix): crust, mantle, core; constructive, destructive and transform boundaries.

objectives.text: Illustrate and describe the internal structure of the Earth.
Outline the continental drift theory and its evidence.
Describe tectonic movement at constructive, destructive and transform plate boundaries.
Explain the implications of plate movements for climate.

children.name: Folding and faulting
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Describe the processes of folding and faulting.
Describe the landforms that result from folding and faulting.

children.name: Volcanoes, earthquakes and the effects of tectonic processes
children.description: Form 3: distribution and causes of volcanoes and earthquakes and their effects.

objectives.text: Outline the distribution of volcanoes and earthquakes.
Explain the causes of volcanoes and earthquakes.
Identify the effects of volcanic activity and earthquakes.

children.name: Landforms resulting from water action and river processes
children.description: Form 4: the seasonal nature of rivers in Zimbabwe; processes along a river channel; valleys, meanders, waterfalls and rapids.

objectives.text: Describe the seasonal nature of water flow in Zimbabwe's rivers.
Explain how river processes shape the landscape.
Describe the landforms that result from river processes.

children.name: Arid and semi-arid regions and landforms resulting from wind action
children.description: Form 4: characteristics and distribution of arid and semi-arid regions; wind erosion, transportation and deposition and the resulting landforms in Zimbabwe and Africa.

objectives.text: Describe the characteristics of arid and semi-arid regions and explain their distribution.
Explain the processes of wind action.
Describe the landforms that result from wind action.

children.name: Hazards associated with landform development and disaster risk management
children.description: Form 3 (measures to reduce the effects of volcanoes and earthquakes) and Form 4 (disaster risk management of volcanoes, earthquakes, flooding and mass wasting).

objectives.text: Describe the hazards associated with landform development.
Identify measures to reduce the effects of volcanic activity and earthquakes.
Identify methods of disaster risk management for volcanoes, earthquakes, flooding and mass wasting.

topics.name: Ecosystems
topics.description: Topic 3 of the scope and sequence: components and interdependence (Form 1), biodiversity, biomes and sustainable management (Form 2), cycles, wetlands, conservation and benefits (Form 3), soils (Form 4).

children.name: Components of ecosystems, micro-ecosystems and interdependence
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: Describe systems and ecosystems and identify their biotic and abiotic components.
Identify the inputs, processes and outputs of a local micro-ecosystem and explain the links between them.
Draw and interpret food chains, food webs and food pyramids.

children.name: Biodiversity, benefits of ecosystems and ecosystems in entrepreneurship
children.description: Form 2 (biodiversity; use of ecosystems in entrepreneurship) and Form 3 (benefits of ecosystems).

objectives.text: Identify habitats in a local ecosystem and the kinds of biodiversity.
Explain the importance and benefits of ecosystems.
Identify and plan small businesses that use local ecosystems sustainably.

children.name: Tropical ecosystems (biomes)
children.description: Form 2: equatorial rainforest, tropical continental (savanna) and tropical desert.

objectives.text: Locate the tropical biomes of Africa.
Identify the inputs, processes and outputs of each biome.
Explain how vegetation and animals are adapted in each biome.

children.name: Sustainable management, conservation and restoration of ecosystems
children.description: Form 2 (sustainable management: fireguards, tree planting, erosion control) and Form 3 (conservation and restoration methods).

objectives.text: Describe the sustainability of ecosystems and strategies for conserving local forests.
Identify methods of conserving ecosystems.
Explain methods of restoring degraded ecosystems and their benefits.

children.name: Biogeochemical cycles
children.description: Form 3: nutrient, nitrogen and carbon cycles.

objectives.text: Explain the nutrient, nitrogen and carbon cycles.
Outline the importance of biogeochemical cycles in ecosystems.

children.name: Wetlands
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Explain the importance of wetlands and outline their benefits.

children.name: Soils
children.description: Form 4: soil components, soil-forming processes in the tropics, soil properties, soil types and profiles.

objectives.text: Identify, measure and analyse the components of soil.
Describe the soil-forming processes of gleying and cheluviation and name the soils they form in the tropics.
Explain soil profiles and describe soil properties and horizons.

topics.name: Natural resources
topics.description: Topic 4 of the scope and sequence (Forms 1 to 3).

children.name: Natural resources, population and the exploitation of resources
children.description: Form 1 (the concept of natural resources; renewable and non-renewable resources; sustainable use in the local area) and Form 2 (population and resources; exploitation of resources in Zimbabwe and Africa).

objectives.text: Classify resources into renewable and non-renewable.
Describe how resources can be extracted sustainably in the local area.
Describe population growth and its effects on resources.
Describe the factors that influence the exploitation of natural resources.

children.name: Conservation of resources
children.description: Form 3: fish, water, soil and forest.

objectives.text: Describe resource conservation measures and identify ways of conserving fish, water, soil and forest resources.

children.name: Wildlife management, human-wildlife conflict and CAMPFIRE
children.description: Form 3: game parks, conservancies, safari areas, sanctuaries and national parks; human-wildlife conflict; the Communal Areas Management Programme for Indigenous Resources (CAMPFIRE), with a Zimbabwean case study.

objectives.text: Describe wildlife management and identify its advantages.
Distinguish problem animals from dangerous animals and explain the causes of and solutions to human-wildlife conflict.
Give reasons for the establishment of CAMPFIRE and discuss its benefits and sustainability.

topics.name: Energy and power development
topics.description: Topic 5 of the scope and sequence (Forms 1 to 3).

children.name: Types, sources and economic importance of energy
children.description: Form 1 (types and sources of energy) and Form 2 (economic importance of energy types; relative importance of different sources).

objectives.text: List types of energy, identify their sources and describe their uses.
Explain the importance of energy in economic activities.
Examine the advantages and disadvantages of different types of energy and justify the choice of a particular type.

children.name: Siting of power plants, power generation and environmental impact
children.description: Form 1: siting of power plants and hydro-electric power; thermal (coal, gas, geothermal), solar, HEP, wind and nuclear generation; pollution, deforestation and climate change, and mitigation.

objectives.text: State the factors that affect the siting of power plants and describe their siting.
Describe types of power generation and explain the processes involved.
Explain the environmental impact of generating and using energy and outline measures to reduce it.

children.name: Conservation of energy sources
children.description: Form 3: energy conservation methods; production and conservation of energy in the local area (project).

objectives.text: Explain how energy sources can be conserved.
Analyse the types of energy used and the conservation measures taken in the local area.

topics.name: Map work and geographical information systems
topics.description: Topic 6 of the scope and sequence: map skills (Form 1), contours, gradient and land use (Form 2), GPS, time zones and remote sensing (Form 3), Boolean logic and overlay analysis (Form 4).

children.name: Characteristics and types of maps and universal symbols
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: List and identify the components of a good map.
Outline the characteristics of the major types of maps and classify maps.
Draw and interpret universal symbols on maps.

children.name: Location: coordinates, grid references and world time zones
children.description: Form 1 (geographic coordinates and the Universal Transverse Mercator grid; a sketch map of home and school) and Form 3 (world time zones).

objectives.text: Determine the latitude and longitude of a point in degrees.
Give the position of a point using grid references in metres.
Calculate time using longitude.

children.name: Scale, distance and area
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: Explain the concept and importance of scale and distinguish among the types of scale.
Use scale to draw simple maps.
Measure straight and winding distances, including with Pythagoras' theorem.
Estimate area on maps using grid squares and graph paper.

children.name: Direction and bearing
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: Explain the concept of direction and illustrate compass directions.
Calculate bearings and navigate using a magnetic compass.

children.name: Contour lines and their interpretation
children.description: Form 2.

objectives.text: Describe the concept of contour lines and determine altitude from them.
Identify landforms from contour patterns.

children.name: Gradient
children.description: Form 2.

objectives.text: Describe the concept of gradient and calculate the gradient of a slope.
Apply gradient data to explain features on a map.

children.name: Land use, patterns and networks on maps
children.description: Form 2: types of land use, factors behind land-use patterns, point, line and area data.

objectives.text: Describe types of land use on a map and explain what determines them.
Identify and describe land-use patterns on a map and the processes that influence them.

children.name: The electromagnetic spectrum and remote sensing
children.description: Form 3: light as a wave, the visible bands of the electromagnetic spectrum and photograph interpretation.

objectives.text: Describe light as a wave and explain the visible bands of the electromagnetic spectrum.
Apply knowledge of the electromagnetic spectrum to interpret photographs.

children.name: GPS and GIS: Boolean logic and overlay analysis
children.description: Form 3 (the Global Positioning System and navigation) and Form 4 (Boolean logic with Venn diagrams; overlay analysis). The Form 4 competency matrix numbers this topic 'Topic 5: Geographic Information Systems (GIS)'.

objectives.text: Explain the concept of GPS and use GPS to navigate.
Describe the basic functions of Boolean logic and apply them to simple spatial problems.
Describe overlay analysis and apply relational and conditional statements in it.

topics.name: Minerals and mining
topics.description: Topic 7 of the scope and sequence (Forms 1 to 4).

children.name: Distribution, groups and importance of minerals in Zimbabwe
children.description: Form 1: geological formations; mines and minerals and their distribution; precious minerals; ores and mineral groups; economic importance.

objectives.text: Identify mines and minerals in Zimbabwe and describe their distribution.
List precious minerals and identify ores and mineral groups.
Describe the economic importance of minerals to Zimbabwe.

children.name: Factors influencing mining and methods of mining
children.description: Form 2: surface and underground methods.

objectives.text: Describe the term mining and the factors that influence mining in Zimbabwe.
Describe surface and underground mining methods and their advantages and disadvantages.

children.name: Mineralogy, gold panning and small-scale mining
children.description: Form 2 (prospecting including indigenous knowledge, properties of alluvial minerals, gold panning) and Form 3 (small-scale mining and the legislative framework on mining rights).

objectives.text: Identify methods used in prospecting for gold and describe the properties of alluvial minerals.
Outline the problems of gold panning and suggest how its contribution to the economy could be increased.
Describe small-scale mining, its contribution to Zimbabwe's economy, its challenges and solutions.
Outline the legislative framework on mining and mining rights.

children.name: Extraction, processing, beneficiation and value addition
children.description: Form 3: processing of selected minerals in Zimbabwe and Africa; beneficiation.

objectives.text: Explain how selected minerals are processed in Zimbabwe and Africa.
Describe the importance of beneficiation of minerals in Zimbabwe.

children.name: Mining, the environment, safety and sustainable use
children.description: Form 2 (environmental impacts of mining and rehabilitation), Form 3 (health and safety in mining) and Form 4 (sustainable use of mineral resources, environmental impact assessment in mining, cost-benefit analysis).

objectives.text: Describe the environmental impacts of mining and identify mitigation and rehabilitation measures.
Explain the importance of safety and health in mining.
Explain the sustainable use of mineral resources.
Explain cost-benefit analysis and its importance in mining.

topics.name: Environmental management
topics.description: Topic 8 of the scope and sequence (Forms 1 to 4). The Form 4 competency matrix numbers it 'Topic 7'.

children.name: The environment, environmental legislation and international protocols
children.description: Form 1 (aspects and state of the environment; environmental management), Form 3 (environmental management legislation) and Forms 3 to 4 (international protocols and treaties and their domestication).

objectives.text: Identify and describe aspects of the environment and distinguish pristine from degraded environments.
Explain environmental management and outline indigenous knowledge systems in it.
Explain environmental management legislation in Zimbabwe and assess its effectiveness, challenges and solutions.
Identify international treaties and protocols on the environment and discuss the pros and cons of domesticating them.

children.name: Environmental deterioration
children.description: Form 2: veld fires, soil erosion, siltation, gullies, uncontrolled mining and sand abstraction, deforestation, wetland destruction, water and air pollution, poor waste management, noise and graffiti.

objectives.text: Describe the forms and causes of environmental degradation.
Explain the social, economic and physical effects of environmental degradation.
Outline measures to reduce environmental degradation.

children.name: Global warming and climate change: impacts, adaptation and mitigation
children.description: Form 2: impact of climate change on land, water and air, positive and negative; climate change adaptation and mitigation.

objectives.text: Identify the impacts of climate change on the environment.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of climate change.
Describe climate change mitigation measures.

children.name: Environmental management planning, EIA and land-use planning
children.description: Form 4. Land-use zoning (Form 1, under Agriculture) and rural and urban land-use planning legislation (Form 1, under Settlement) are taught with this concept.

objectives.text: Describe environmental management planning and the environmental impact assessment process.
Describe land-use planning in Zimbabwe and explain it as a strategy for sustainable environmental management.
Identify challenges in land-use planning and suggest mitigation measures.

topics.name: Agriculture and land reform
topics.description: Topic 9 of the scope and sequence (Forms 1 to 4). The Form 4 competency matrix numbers it 'Topic 8'.

children.name: Factors influencing agriculture, farming as a system and land-use zoning
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: Explain agriculture, identify its types and explain the factors that influence it.
Name the elements of a farm and classify inputs into physical, human and economic.
Identify land-use zones in a community and justify the need for zoning.

children.name: Farming types in Zimbabwe
children.description: Form 2: subsistence and communal farming; commercial dairying, horticulture and market gardening, cattle ranching, mixed farming, plantation and irrigation farming.

objectives.text: Identify the dominant farming types in Zimbabwe.
Explain the characteristics, benefits and challenges of each farming type.

children.name: Agro-ecological regions of Zimbabwe
children.description: Form 2: location, characteristics and farming activities of each region. The document lists 'Regions 1 - 6' (see notes).

objectives.text: Draw Zimbabwe's agro-ecological regions on a map.
Describe the characteristics of each region and explain its farming activities.

children.name: Land tenure and land reform in Zimbabwe
children.description: Form 3: freehold, leasehold, communal and state land; land consolidation and fragmentation; resettlement phases and models.

objectives.text: Describe land tenure systems in Zimbabwe and compare their advantages and disadvantages.
Describe and explain forms of land reform and the reasons for land reform in Zimbabwe.
Explain the land reform process in Zimbabwe, its outcomes and challenges.

children.name: Small-scale farmers and food security
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Outline the contribution of small-scale farming to food security.

children.name: Climate change and agriculture; agricultural diseases and pests
children.description: Form 4.

objectives.text: Deduce the effects of climate change on agriculture and suggest mitigation and adaptation measures.
Identify agricultural pests and diseases and describe their effects.
Suggest manual, biological and chemical control measures.

children.name: Urban agriculture and agribusiness
children.description: Form 4.

objectives.text: Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of urban agriculture and suggest solutions to its problems.
List types of agribusiness in Zimbabwe and identify sources of funding for small-scale agribusiness.
Evaluate the importance of agribusiness to the individual and the economy.

topics.name: Industry
topics.description: Topic 10 of the scope and sequence (Forms 1 to 4). The Form 4 competency matrix numbers it 'Topic 9'.

children.name: Types of industry and their importance to Zimbabwe
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: Describe industry and identify types of industry.
Explain the importance of industries to Zimbabwe.

children.name: Factors influencing the location of industry
children.description: Form 2 (secondary industry).

objectives.text: Explain the factors that influence the location of industries.

children.name: Manufacturing and processing industries in Zimbabwe
children.description: Form 1 (nature and distribution of industries in Zimbabwe), Form 2 (types and distribution of manufacturing and processing industries) and Form 3 (problems facing manufacturing and processing industries).

objectives.text: Describe the distribution of industries in Zimbabwe.
Discuss examples of manufacturing and processing industries.
Identify solutions to the challenges facing manufacturing and processing industries in Zimbabwe.

children.name: Transnational corporations
children.description: Form 2.

objectives.text: Describe transnational corporations and discuss their advantages and disadvantages.

children.name: Small to medium enterprises, informal industries and occupational safety and health
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Describe the causes, characteristics and location of small to medium enterprises.
Discuss the role of informal industries in Zimbabwe.
Discuss measures adopted in industries to promote occupational safety and health.

children.name: Service industries, tourism and quaternary industries
children.description: Form 4: tourism as a case study of a service industry; tourism in Zimbabwe; quaternary industries; problems of service industries.

objectives.text: Describe service industries and quaternary industries in Zimbabwe.
Define tourism and describe tourism in Zimbabwe and its importance.
Describe the problems of tourism and other service industries in Zimbabwe and suggest solutions.

topics.name: Settlement and population
topics.description: Topic 11 of the scope and sequence: rural settlement (Form 1), urbanisation (Form 2), population data and distribution (Form 3), population change, migration, policy and disease (Form 4). The Form 4 competency matrix numbers it 'Topic 10'.

children.name: Types, site and situation of settlements and rural settlement patterns
children.description: Form 1 (types of settlement, site and situation, rural settlement patterns, rural and urban land-use planning legislation) and Form 2 (disaster-resilient infrastructure).

objectives.text: Identify types of settlement and describe their characteristics.
Distinguish the site and situation of a settlement and identify the site factors of a local settlement.
Identify and describe rural settlement patterns.
List the laws governing rural and urban land use in Zimbabwe.
Identify the features of disaster-resilient infrastructure and the factors considered in siting settlements.

children.name: Urbanisation
children.description: Form 2: causes, process and effects of urbanisation and solutions to its problems.

objectives.text: Explain the causes of urbanisation and describe the process.
Describe the effects of urbanisation.
Suggest solutions to problems of urbanisation.

children.name: Urban land-use zones and models
children.description: Form 2: CBD, industrial, residential and recreational zones; concentric, sector and multiple-nuclei models.

objectives.text: Describe urban land-use zones.
Outline the main features of urban land-use models and match them to towns in Zimbabwe.

children.name: Unplanned urban settlements
children.description: Form 2.

objectives.text: State the characteristics of unplanned settlements and describe their location in urban centres.
Explain the causes and outline the effects of unplanned settlements.
Suggest measures to solve the problems of unplanned settlements.

children.name: Population terms
children.description: Form 3: birth rate, death rate, infant mortality rate, fertility.

objectives.text: Describe population terms and apply them at local and national levels.

children.name: Population data collection, presentation and interpretation
children.description: Form 3: sample surveys and school census; presentation techniques; population pyramids (for example Zimbabwe compared with Sweden or Germany).

objectives.text: Collect population data within the school or local community.
Analyse and present population data.
Interpret population data, including population pyramids.

children.name: Population distribution and density
children.description: Form 3: Zimbabwe, Africa and the world.

objectives.text: Describe population distribution in Zimbabwe, Africa and the world.
Explain differences in population density.

children.name: Population growth and the demographic transition model
children.description: Form 4: factors affecting growth; the DTM and its critique; effects of population growth and decline.

objectives.text: Identify and explain the factors that influence population growth.
Describe the features of the stages of the demographic transition model.
Identify countries with high and low population growth and explain the effects of growth and decline.

children.name: Causes and effects of migration
children.description: Form 4: push and pull factors; effects in sending and receiving areas; internal and international, voluntary and involuntary migration.

objectives.text: Describe the causes of migration.
Explain the effects of migration.
Outline the different categories of migration.

children.name: Population policy
children.description: Form 4.

objectives.text: Describe the rationale for population policies.
Explain the effects of population policies in named developed and developing countries.

children.name: Population and diseases
children.description: Form 4.

objectives.text: Describe diseases associated with developing and developed countries.
Explain the differences in diseases between developed and developing countries.
Explain the social and economic effects of diseases.

topics.name: Transport and trade
topics.description: Topic 12 of the scope and sequence (Forms 1 to 3).

children.name: Modes of transport
children.description: Form 1: air, rail, road, water and pipeline.

objectives.text: Describe transport and identify its modes.
Explain changes in modes of transport and their advantages and disadvantages.

children.name: Transport networks and transport challenges
children.description: Form 1: networks in Zimbabwe, the region and Africa; transport indices; flow-line diagrams.

objectives.text: Explain the transport networks of Zimbabwe, the region and Africa and draw them.
Calculate and interpret transport indices.
Discuss solutions to transport challenges.

children.name: Trade, regional imbalances and trading blocs
children.description: Form 2 (trade; domestic and foreign trade; trade patterns of Zimbabwe, SADC, Africa and the world) and Form 3 (regional imbalances in trade; SADC, COMESA, ECOWAS, OPEC, EU).

objectives.text: Explain trade and describe trade patterns in Zimbabwe, SADC, Africa and the world.
Outline the characteristics of domestic and foreign trade and distinguish them.
Show how trading patterns create imbalances nationally and between regions.
Name economic groupings and give reasons for the formation of trading blocs.
